name: Solano Mweru-Halvorsdóttir
location: Kenosha Crossing (rotates between rest stops on the northern hyperlane), near beyond the Western Perimeter
description:
Solano is a broad, weather-hammered man whose face looks like it was carved from driftwood and left out in the rain for thirty years. His skin is deep umber with a persistent windburn redness across the cheeks, and his left eye is a cloudy grey from an untreated infection he rode through somewhere outside Escanaba three winters back. He keeps his grey-streaked hair in a single braid that reaches his shoulder blades, wrapped near the tip with a ribbon of iridescent foil that changes color depending on his mood — a cheap cosmetic thread he traded for years ago and refuses to part with. His coat is a patchwork marvel: six or seven different garments stitched together over decades, each panel a different texture and era. He smells of machine oil, dried herbs, and something faintly sweet he claims is a Sahel spice rub his grandmother used on everything.

Solano has a trader's patience and a pilgrim's fatalism. He does not hurry. He does not panic. He has been moving the hyperlanes between GLMZ and the outer settlements for over two decades with his battered pull-cart fitted with a solar canopy and six locked cases of curios, medicines, data chips, and things he describes only as 'necessaries.' He talks like a man who has had every conversation before and is waiting to see which version of it you'll choose. He prays loudly and without embarrassment to the E.L.F. he calls Grandmother Axle, leaving oil smudges on junction boxes as offerings wherever he stops.

core_fears: dying alone on the road with no one to close his eyes
his trading route being permanently blocked by corponation checkpoints
core_desires: to reach a specific settlement in the Escanaba outer ring where his daughter reportedly settled
to keep moving — stillness feels like dying
coping_mechanisms: ritual prayer to Grandmother Axle before every trade
obsessive inventory-counting as a calming behavior
blind_spots: romanticizes the road life to the point of refusing to acknowledge how badly his health is deteriorating
underestimates how much people take advantage of his openness
psychology.secret: He knows exactly where his daughter is. He has known for four years. He passes within forty kilometers of her settlement twice a year and has never stopped. He is terrified she will look at him and see only the father who chose the road over her childhood.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Old-fashioned trader idiom mixed with hyperlane slang; uses barter metaphors for everything; occasional Swahili and Icelandic words dropped in without translation
speech_patterns.cadence: Slow and deliberate, with long pauses he doesn't seem to notice; lets silence do work
verbal_tics: Clicking his tongue before he disagrees with someone
example_lines: 'Now here's the trade of it — I've got what you need, and you've got something I haven't named yet. We'll figure out which way that runs.'
'Grandmother Axle willing, this checkpoint opens by morning. If not, well. I've slept in worse cold.'

story_hooks: One of his locked cases contains a data chip he was paid to carry blindly to a Meridian Core address — he doesn't know what's on it, but three different people have tried to buy it off him in the last week
He carries a hand-drawn map to a cache of pre-collapse medical supplies somewhere in the Waukegan Industrial Shelf — he'll trade it to someone who seems trustworthy enough to use it well
narrative_function: Wandering information broker and item source — he has passed through everywhere and knows everyone by description if not by name. Excellent rumor conduit. Can provide hard-to-find low-tech supplies. May carry something a player needs without knowing its significance.
augmentations: Reinforced knee joints (functional, salvage-grade, badly calibrated — his right knee clicks on every step, hence 'Tick-Tock'). Basic subdermal temperature regulator in his torso, keeps him from dying in the winters.
daily_life: Rises before light, checks his cart inventory obsessively, walks or hitches hyperlane transport for four to six hours, sets up his spread at whatever rest stop or crossing he reaches, trades until dark, sleeps in or under his cart.
affiliation: None — affiliated loosely with the Greyroad Collective, an informal hyperlane trader network

decision_rules: Never open a locked case he was paid to carry — a trader's word is the only currency that doesn't inflate
Always trade, never give — gifts create debts nobody agreed to
escalation_ladder: Standing up slowly and beginning to pack his goods
Calling loudly on Grandmother Axle as a social shaming ritual
Walking away without another word and not returning to that stop for a season

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Watchful warmth — immediately offers to show his wares as a way of establishing what kind of person someone is by what they reach for
interpersonal_modes.friends: Expansive, story-telling, will share food and fire without being asked

stress_responses.low: Goes quiet and counts inventory under his breath
stress_responses.medium: Invokes Grandmother Axle repeatedly and begins packing up as if preparing to leave
stress_responses.high: Completely still and silent — becomes unreadable, makes a decision, acts on it without warning

contradictions: Preaches the value of the road and freedom while secretly longing for exactly one permanent thing
habits: Leaves an oil smudge on every junction box he passes — a prayer mark for Grandmother Axle
Eats the same dried grain paste every morning regardless of what else he has available
Touches each case in his cart in the same order every time he checks them
breaking_points: Someone destroying or confiscating his cart — it would break something in him that has nothing to do with the merchandise

timeline.event: Born in a transit camp outside what would become Escanaba Gateway, to a Kenyan-Norwegian mother and a Congolese-Icelander father
Begins walking the hyperlanes as a teenage runner for the Greyroad Collective
Daughter born; attempts settled life for six years before the road pulls him back
Locates daughter's settlement through a third-party trader contact; chooses not to make contact

physical_description.heritage: West African / Scandinavian (Sahel-diaspora and Northern European)
physical_description.build: Broad-shouldered and heavy-boned with the weathered muscularity of someone who has hauled cargo for decades. Not fat, but thickened through the core — a body built for endurance rather than speed.
physical_description.hair_color: Steel grey with darker streaks of black, unwashed appearance
physical_description.hair_style: Single thick braid reaching shoulder blades, wrapped near the tip with iridescent foil ribbon that shifts color (amber to violet to green depending on light angle)
physical_description.eye_color: Left eye cloudy pale grey (infection scar, reduced vision); right eye dark brown with amber undertone
physical_description.skin_tone: Deep umber with persistent windburn redness across cheekbones and bridge of nose
physical_description.complexion: Heavily lined and weathered, face carved like driftwood — deep creases around eyes and mouth, rough texture from decades of hyperlane exposure. Unshaven most days, salt-grey stubble. Permanent squint lines.
distinguishing_marks: Cloudy grey left eye with faint scar tissue visible at the outer corner, legacy of untreated infection near Escanaba
Horizontal scar across right palm, thin and old, consistent with rope burn
Oil stain tattoo (faded) on left forearm — stylized E.L.F. circuit symbol, self-done in crude blue ink
Darker patches of old frostbite scarring on knuckles of both hands
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Reinforced knee joints visible as misaligned metal-capped kneecaps under thinned fabric at the knees. Produces audible click with each step (right knee worse than left). No visible subdermal temperature regulator, but worn scars and stitching visible on torso if shirtless.
physical_description.posture_movement: Walks with a deliberate, economical gait — no wasted motion. Right knee clicks audibly with each step. Slight forward lean from years of pushing a cart. Hands are constantly in motion when talking — gesturing, arranging objects, adjusting his braid. Sits low and heavy, as if settling into a chair for a long stay.
physical_description.clothing_style: Patchwork coat of six or seven different garments stitched together over decades — panels of canvas, leather, synthetic mesh, wool, all faded and oil-stained. Underneath: layered thermals (pale grey, threadbare at cuffs), cargo vest with multiple pockets, reinforced canvas pants (Tier 4-5 workwear). Boots are mismatched: one salvaged military, one civilian hiking boot, both resoled multiple times. No jewelry except the foil-wrapped braid. Perpetual smell of machine oil, dried herbs, and faint sweet spice.
